title: Samosa

seo.title: Authentic Pakistani Samosa Recipe - Crispy & Flavorful
seo.metaDescription: Master the art of making authentic Pakistani Samosa recipe at home! Get crispy, flavorful Samosas with our easy step-by-step guide. Perfect appetizer for any occasion.
h2Headings: How to Store and Reheat Samosas
seo.imageAlt: Plate of golden-brown, crispy authentic Pakistani Samosa recipe served with chutney.
seo.imageCaption: Enjoy these perfectly fried, authentic Pakistani Samosas – a delightful appetizer for any gathering!

description: Samosas are a quintessential Pakistani snack, beloved for their crispy pastry shell and savory spiced filling. These golden triangles are perfect as an appetizer, a tea-time treat, or a delightful snack for any occasion. Our recipe brings you the authentic taste of Pakistani Samosas, ensuring a burst of flavor in every bite.

instructions.title: Prepare the Samosa Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine all-purpose flour, salt, and carom seeds. Add 4 tablespoons of ghee or oil and rub it into the flour until it resembles breadcrumbs. Gradually add water and knead into a firm, non-sticky dough. Cover with a damp cloth and let it rest for at least 20 minutes.

instructions.title: Cook the Samosa Filling
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan. Add chopped onions and saute until translucent. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook for a minute until fragrant. Stir in coriander powder, cumin powder, red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, and amchur (if using). Cook spices for 30 seconds, then add green peas and a splash of water, cooking until peas are tender. Add the mashed potatoes and fresh coriander leaves, mix well, and season with salt. Cook for 2-3 minutes, then let the filling cool completely.

instructions.title: Roll out the Dough
instructions.text: Divide the rested dough into equal small balls, about the size of a golf ball. Take one ball and roll it into an oval shape, about 6-7 inches long and 4 inches wide. Cut the oval in half lengthwise to create two semi-circles.

instructions.title: Shape and Fill the Samosas
instructions.text: Take one semi-circle. Moisten the straight edge with water. Bring the two ends of the straight edge together to form a cone shape, pressing firmly to seal. Fill the cone with 1-2 tablespoons of the cooled potato filling. Moisten the top edges of the cone with water, then pinch and pleat one side while pressing the other side straight onto it to seal the Samosa into a triangular shape. Ensure it's tightly sealed to prevent filling from leaking.

instructions.title: Repeat and Prepare for Frying
instructions.text: Continue shaping and filling the remaining dough and filling. Place the shaped Samosas on a tray, ensuring they do not stick together. You can prepare these ahead and refrigerate for a few hours or freeze for longer storage.

instructions.title: Fry the Samosas to Golden Perfection
instructions.text: Heat oil for deep frying in a heavy-bottomed pan or wok over medium-low heat. The oil should not be too hot, as this will make the Samosas bubbly and not crispy. Gently slide the Samosas into the warm oil, frying them in batches without overcrowding the pan. Fry on medium-low heat for 12-15 minutes, turning occasionally, until they are golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain excess oil on paper towels.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Serve the authentic Pakistani Samosas hot with your favorite chutney, such as mint chutney, tamarind chutney, or ketchup. Enjoy this crispy, flavorful appetizer!

tips: For truly crispy Samosas, ensure your dough is firm and kneaded well. The amount of ghee or oil rubbed into the flour (moen) is crucial for a flaky crust. Fry on medium-low heat to ensure even cooking and maximum crispiness.
The filling should be completely cool before you start filling the Samosas. Warm filling can make the dough soggy and harder to handle, leading to less crispy Samosas.

If making ahead, you can freeze un-fried Samosas on a tray until solid, then transfer them to a freezer bag. Fry from frozen, adding a few extra minutes to the cooking time, for a quick and fresh snack anytime.
